pass-by-value.why: Java passes copies. bump(int) changes its own copy of a. bump(int[]) gets a copy of the reference, which still points at the same array, so the change shows. replace only points its own copy somewhere else, so the caller's array is untouched.

how-java-passes.why: Everything is passed by value. For an object, the value is a reference, so the method can change the object it points to but can't make the caller's variable point at a different object.

overload-static-type.why: Overloads are chosen at compile time from the declared (static) type of the argument. o is declared Object, so describe(Object) is chosen even though it holds a String. (Overriding, by contrast, is decided at run time.)

builder-through-method.why: add changes the object both references point at. swap only reassigns its own parameter, which the caller never sees.

loop-scope.why: A local variable's scope ends at the closing brace of the block that declares it. Declare it before the loop if you need it afterwards.

return-early.why: Parameters first; then the loop; the check returns as soon as it finds the target; -1 is returned only after every index has been checked.
